videos.script: An animation in SwiftUI is not something you start. The state changes at once, and the animation is how the screen travels to it. {{two}} You can ask for one in two places. On the view, for one value it watches. Or around the change, for everything the change touches. {{numbers}} Then what actually moves. SwiftUI animates numbers: a width, an opacity, an angle. Your body runs once, and SwiftUI fills in the frames. {{curves}} Those frames follow a curve, and a curve is arithmetic. So you compute four of them on your own machine, and the spring that has been the default since iOS 17. {{transitions}} Then views that arrive and leave, which are not interpolated at all. They get transitions. {{matched}} One view that seems to move between two places. {{reduce}} And the setting some people need, because movement on a screen makes them ill. The SwiftUI half is written from Apple's documentation, and the lesson says so.
